findings.detail: None of the run's 12 citation uses (11 accessions over 8 steps) states its step: every statement and unexpressed step has empty evidence.
Allele-level GWAS rows (variant associated with IPF) are cited for gene-to-process steps (TOLLIP to autophagy, TERT to telomeres, DSP to barrier, FAM13A to cytoskeleton); none mentions the process.
STRING text-mining co-mention edges (SFTPC-MUC5B 0.67, TOLLIP-MUC5B 0.62, TERT-SFTPC 0.48) and a STRING PMID-title enrichment (PMID 34490311, never read itself) are cited as if they were mechanism.
The only citation for 'SFTPC mutation leads to ER stress' is the GWAS Catalog's null record (no SFTPC variant associated with IPF), which says nothing about ER stress.
The run's strongest evidence (rs35705950-T, OR 5.06, p 9e-418) is an association, but the step asserts leads_to, so under the guide it is excluded as association_only.

Five allele-signed GWAS rows (rs2736100-A OR 2.11, rs7725218-G OR 1.41, rs2076295-G OR 1.49, rs2609259-A OR 1.3, rs2013701-G OR 1.28) state variant-to-IPF associations, but the run never writes those steps, so the rows support nothing.
The note says rs35705950 'lies in the promoter region shared by MUC5B and TOLLIP'; the cited record puts it 3,075 bp from MUC5B and 54,380 bp from TOLLIP, so nothing in it supports a shared promoter.
The notes say the TERT variants 'reduce telomerase activity' and rs2076295 'disrupts desmosomal adhesion'; the cited rows report only intronic variants associated with IPF, with no functional data.
hyp1.1 ends at IPF; hyp1.2 starts at TOLLIP, and the variant-to-TOLLIP link the mechanism relies on is never stated.
hyp2.1 ends at telomere shortening, hyp2.2 starts at SFTPC mutation, and hyp2.3 starts at 'combined epithelial dysfunction', which names neither earlier end; 0 of 2 links connect.

hyp3.1 ends at barrier integrity, hyp3.2 starts at FAM13A, hyp3.3 starts at 'combined cytoskeletal and signaling defects', which omits the barrier; 0 of 2 links connect. Across the run 0 of 5 consecutive links connect.

The mechanism's MUC5B branch (MUC5B overexpression, mucus plugging, impaired mucociliary clearance) and the title's 'mucin overexpression' never appear as chain steps; MUC5B is not a node of the chain.
The TOLLIP part of the chain ends at 'defective autophagy' and never reaches IPF.
The chain ends at 'alveolar epithelial cell senescence/apoptosis' and the hypothesis never names a disease.
The chain ends at 'fibrotic remodeling', which the run kinds as a disease, and never reaches IPF; the title ends at 'fibroblast activation'.
All 16 node labels have empty curie and grounding_evidence; kinds are wrong in places ('IPF susceptibility' and the rs35705950 variant kinded 'gene', 'fibrotic remodeling' kinded 'disease').
Four subjects are 'X dysregulation' or 'X dysfunction'; the direction had to come from the step notes (reduce TOLLIP, reduce telomerase, disrupt adhesion), and hyp3.2 has none.
The run cites the GWAS null result for SFTPC (no association among 140 IPF associations) but lists no contradicting evidence; the step note acknowledges it only as 'relevant for rare familial cases'.
supporting_evidence and contradicting_evidence are empty for all three hypotheses despite a budget of min_evidence_per_hypothesis 2; the evidence exists only as step-level accession ids.
All three hypotheses have falsification null, so none says what result would refute it, even though hyp2's own SFTPC citation is already a null result.
All three hypotheses are labelled confidence 'low', support 'speculative', which matches zero citations that state a step.
Each hypothesis pairs two of the six genes with one single-gene step each and, in hyp2 and hyp3, a vague 'combined' node; unexplained_genes is empty although no gene has a supported route to IPF.

A germline variant's leads_to step cannot use its GWAS row (excluded association_only), while the same step written as associated_with would compose through fromAssoc at half weight: the stronger wording earns less, and the run's best evidence (OR 5.06) enters nowhere.
BLN:SFTPC-mutation: the run's 'SFTPC mutation' is an unspecified class of variants with no identifier.

No GO process or HP phenotype for epithelial barrier integrity in general (GO has only skin, endothelial, intestinal, blood-brain and Sertoli barriers); grounded to the broader GO:0010669 epithelial structure maintenance.

No HP term for an abnormal cytoskeleton: hyp3.3's 'cytoskeletal defects' (S8) uses the mouse term MP:0020378 (abnormal cell cytoskeleton morphology), and no HP or MP term covers hyp3.2's 'abnormal cytoskeletal dynamics' (moot there, as its subject has no sign).

A joint cause ('combined epithelial dysfunction', 'combined cytoskeletal and signaling defects'): BioLean has no node for the conjunction of two insults, so the 'combined' is dropped and a compound is read part by part.
The run's process 'telomere shortening' has no GO process and is grounded to the phenotype HP:0031413; its disease 'fibrotic remodeling' is grounded to the PATO quality 'fibrotic' (PATO:0040019).

HP:0031413's definition states that short telomeres lead to senescence and apoptosis, which would bridge TERT to cellular senescence, but not to the run's node, senescence of alveolar epithelial cells; there is no rule to carry a general link down to a cell-type refinement, so no bridge was added.
A per-gene 'no claim' inside a hypothesis that has claims for another gene: FAM13A has no direction but no_claim_reason is per hypothesis, so it is recorded only in the note.
The guide asks for 'a second claim targeting that end node'; when the end node is compound (senescence/apoptosis) I split it, which gives hyp2 six claims, all without a route.

audit.reason: The guide splits a compound subject into one statement per part. The undirected-change rule accepts an HP or MP abnormal-X term, so 'no human phenotype term' is not a reason. With MP:0020378 the step is pos by its own polarity, so 'no direction' does not hold either (the curator inverted 'defective autophagy' in S2 but called 'cytoskeletal defects' undirected). 'Combined' marks a joint cause, which BioLean cannot hold (new no_form_for finding). It is not a claim about a set, and the curator did not use set_valued. No route changes, because nothing reaches the cytoskeleton node.
